newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Kuehbacher: France Telecom decision wrong.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Kuehbacher: France Telecom decision wrong.

text.p: German Bundesbank council member Klaus-Dieter Kuehbacher said on Thursday he thought the European Commission's decision to allow the French government to include a transfer from France Telecom to government funds was wrong.

"I think it is wrong. They are consuming in one sole swoop their assets, and on the other side they have a permanent burden," he told reporters in Hamburg. "It challenges other countries which seemingly do not fulfil the criteria to take similar measures."

The European Commission said earlier on Thursday it would allow France to include a 37.5 billion French franc ($7.34 billion) transfer from the telecom operator to government funds in a move that will allow the country to reduce its 1997 budget deficit.
Kuehbacher, who was earlier speaking at a conference on European monetary union, said the decision ran counter to the principle of ensuring lasting adherence to the Maastricht criteria for EMU entry.
The payment is due to be made in exchange for the French government assuming the state-owned company's pension liabilities.
